audit_findings.title: Convertible-note interest and conversion shares burden the same valuation
audit_findings.magnitude: 20.477 million conversion shares and $9.626 million of FY2025 pre-tax 2029 Notes interest expense
audit_findings.mechanism: The conversion shares increase the per-share denominator while interest on the same notes reduces owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2029 Convertible Notes are convertible based on an initial conversion rate of 89.0313 shares of Class A Common Stock per $1,000 principal amount (equivalent to an initial conversion price of $ 11.232 per share).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-basis mismatch. The denominator assumes conversion of the 2029 Notes, but the $35.7 million owner-earnings anchor retains the notes' interest burden. The conversion shares equal 24.4% of the 83.901 million fully diluted share count, and the retained pre-tax interest equals 27.0% of the anchor, so the inconsistency is material.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on two internally consistent bases: converted, with the 2029 Notes' after-tax interest and financing-cost amortization added back; and unconverted, without the 20.477 million conversion shares and using the prescribed unconverted-debt treatment.

audit_findings.title: The post-acquisition minority claim is missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.123 million NCI at 2026-06-30; July 2026 buyout consideration unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An NCI deduction belongs in the equity bridge while outstanding; after its purchase, the consideration paid instead reduces cash attributable to EZCORP shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: They include the accounts of EZCORP, Inc., and its wholly-owned subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The June balance sheet demonstrates a $3.123 million NCI claim, equal to only 0.36% of the $878 million base equity value. However, EZCORP acquired the remaining 2.6% of SMG in July, before the valuation date, and the consideration is not supplied. Thus the minority claim itself was subsequently extinguished, but the June cash bridge may overstate value by omitting the post-balance-sheet payment; its materiality cannot be established from this record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 2026 SMG buyout consideration and payment terms, roll June cash and liabilities forward for the transaction, remove the $3.123 million NCI balance, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Pre-SMG owner earnings are paired with a post-SMG balance sheet
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.7 million of SMG income before tax from 2026-01-02 through 2026-06-30 versus the $35.7 million FY2025 owner-earnings anchor; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator excludes post-acquisition SMG operations while the cash, debt, assets and other bridge amounts reflect SMG consolidation and acquisition transactions.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, we own a preferred interest in Founders One, LLC (“Founders”) that has majority ownership in Simple Management Group, Inc. (“SMG”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated mixed-perimeter error. The stated January 2, 2026 rerun trigger occurred before both the June balance-sheet date and September valuation date. Filed post-acquisition results were available: SMG contributed $94.4 million of revenue and $14.7 million of pre-tax income through June. Those earnings are large relative to the anchor, while acquisition funding, NCI purchases and consolidation also changed the bridge, so direction is mixed but material.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild owner earnings through June 2026 on the same consolidated perimeter as the bridge, normalizing the partial SMG period, acquisition costs, the $1.6 million remeasurement gain, acquisition financing, intercompany eliminations and NCI attribution; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial year of the new senior-note coupon
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.878 million additional annual contractual interest before tax; $9.145 million net pre-tax after removing $1.733 million of FY2025 2025 Notes expense, before financing-cost amortization
audit_findings.mechanism: Because interest remains in equity-level owner earnings, an incomplete recurring coupon inflates the perpetuated anchor; interest from debt retired during FY2025 has the opposite effect and must be removed.
audit_findings.evidence: In March 2025, we issued $300.0 million aggregate principal amount of the Company’s 7.375% senior notes due 2032 (the “2032 Senior Notes”), for which $300.0 million remains outstanding as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated normalization error. A full $300 million coupon at 7.375% is $22.125 million annually, versus $11.247 million recorded in FY2025, leaving $10.878 million of additional recurring contractual interest. After offsetting the filed $1.733 million FY2025 expense on the retired 2025 Notes, the identified net pre-tax reduction is $9.145 million before normalizing financing-cost amortization—25.6% of the $35.7 million anchor.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor for a full year of 2032 Notes contractual interest and deferred-financing-cost amortization, remove all FY2025 interest and amortization associated with repaid or converted notes, apply the appropriate tax effect, and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: Cash Converters may be valued twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.936 million FY2025 Cash Converters equity income, $3.614 million cash dividends and $65.7 million stakes_net bridge addition
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income may remain in owner earnings while the separately valued Cash Converters stake is also added through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our equity in Cash Converters’ net income was $ 6.9 million and $ 5.0 million in fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error, because the owner-earnings schedule is not supplied. If the $6.936 million equity-method income remains in the $35.7 million anchor, it represents 19.4% of anchor earnings and is capitalized in addition to the $65.7 million stakes bridge amount. That potential scale is material. Cash dividends of $3.614 million require separate treatment to avoid removing genuine cash received while also double counting affiliate earnings.
audit_findings.action: Trace every Cash Converters entry in the FY2025 owner-earnings calculation; remove equity-method income and noncash affiliate adjustments, document the treatment of the $3.614 million dividends, reconcile stakes_net to the June 2026 quoted stake value, and rerun if duplication exists.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be distributable dollar-for-dollar
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.7 million disclosed withholding tax on $133.6 million of undistributed foreign earnings; required operating cash unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash at face value even though repatriation taxes or minimum local operating-liquidity requirements may reduce the amount available to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that, upon distribution of our share of these earnings, we would be subject to withholding taxes of approximately $ 6.7 million as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed $6.7 million withholding exposure is only 0.76% of the $878 million base equity value, or about $0.08 per diluted share, and would not alone be material. However, the record does not identify how much of the $311.026 million June cash balance is foreign or required to fund pawn loans, regulatory liquidity and daily operations. That additional unavailable amount may affect value, but its materiality is unquantified. Separately reported restricted cash is not included in the $311.026 million cash line.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 cash by jurisdiction and legal entity, identify minimum operating and regulatory cash, reconcile indefinitely reinvested earnings to actual cash, apply jurisdiction-specific withholding taxes to amounts assumed distributable, and rerun the bridge if the unavailable total is material.
